current_behavior: When primary is unreadable and backup loads, only keys present in the backup enter recoveredFromBackupKeys.
A session created only in a newer primary and absent from the stale backup is returned as record=null and can be treated as fresh.
When both primary and backup are unreadable, load() silently installs an empty Map and an empty recoveredFromBackupKeys set.
If persistence artifacts existed, this empty state is not proof that all previous sessions safely disappeared; accepted mutating tool calls may have existed in the lost newer state.
Therefore explicit session ids can reach provider work again without QWEN_SESSION_RECOVERY_UNCERTAIN in both cases.

contract: Track store-wide recovery uncertainty if backup is used.
Also track store-wide recovery uncertainty when persistence artifacts existed but neither primary nor backup can be read.
Under store-wide uncertainty, an explicit session key absent from the loaded snapshot is ambiguous and must fail closed before provider work.
Existing recovered keys remain uncertain as before.
An explicit reset/clear is the deliberate local action that authorizes an ambiguous missing key to start fresh.
First-ever startup with no persistence artifacts and a normal readable empty primary keep accepting new session ids.

required_product_regressions: Stale backup lacks session-X; newer primary accepted a pending mutating tool call for session-X; primary corrupts; restart from backup; explicit session-X must fail before provider.
Both primary and backup exist but are unreadable after prior persisted work; restart; arbitrary explicit prior session-X must fail before provider rather than look fresh.
First-ever startup with no persistence artifacts must allow a new explicit session id.
Readable empty primary must allow a new explicit session id.
Explicit reset of an ambiguous missing key must permit a consciously fresh session afterward.
limits: No live provider, Notion, or Codex traffic.
No CircleCI, GitHub Actions, Cloudflare, or other hosted CI.
No production, real accounts, secrets, user data, or native Windows.
